claims.title: Compact periodic locking: finite response, live equilibrium and actual kinetic cost

quoted_fields.interface: Literal H=pY^2/(2B0)+L^2/(2I)+V(phi-gY), compact angle, finite smooth periodic V, counted translating/rotating mass; added spring k=kappa/B and actual finite-band Rubin leads where specified. Fixed-I large-g family, finite pinned regulators before local lead/gain limits. Isolated response additionally needs the declared fresh cosine packet/N=0 stock, isolation switch, controlled normal ramp, finite hold and calibrated finite-aperture qubit meter.
quoted_fields.failure: Band curvature, prepared isolated packet and full Gibbs state are different claims. The sharp response barrier is not proved sufficient for the stronger live dynamical limit. The earlier fixed-P small-flux preparation gate is not automatically valid at b=R log^2 R. Heat requires equilibrium KMS input/output completeness and no unassigned persistent bound memory; those premises and finite Gibbs/NESS preparation remain unproved here. Kinetic bounds are not dissipated heat or an all-mechanical/topology lower bound. Finite material rigidity, pitch, force/bandwidth, switches, field-generator mass/energy and readout are unacquired. Third-party ancestry is cited by the proofs, not republished or independently novelty-cleared.

claims.title: Bounded internal force and finite-energy half-charge canonical memory

quoted_fields.interface: H_G=p^T M^-1 p/2+q^T Kq/2 with constant positive M,K and Y=v^Tq; H=H_G+H_A-lambda QY, ||Q||<=q_*, no mechanical momentum coupling or extra thermal port. C=v^TK^-1v remains bounded before the local lead limit. The canonical extension separately needs the complete rotor H_eta=H_G+E_R(N-1/2-eta)^2-lambda Y(2cos phi), actual half-offset/even force, symmetric charge cutoffs/form limit and the declared fixed spring/temperature parameters.
quoted_fields.failure: The finite-internal bounded-force theorem is not an arbitrary coupling or spin-exclusive theorem; the infinite rotor has its own domain/trace-limit argument. Exact J protection requires eta=0 and its actual symmetry assumptions; cosine bias can break sector pairing and sine defects can break J. The full rotor normal ladder is not a free Pauli doublet; the detuning actuator is unbounded. The rotor result proves equilibrium memory, energy and force, not eta-dependent cold response, the earlier spin heat law, finite Gibbs/NESS preparation or control precision. Conserved static Q can saturate the static bound while supplying no heat scattering. The final intake preserves and statically reads the diagnostic scripts; numerical outputs remain source-reported and were not replayed or whole-code audited. No measured device, priority or practical advantage is established.
